name: Margaret River
label: left
text: Surrounded on three sides by the Indian and Southern oceans, Margaret River's mild, even climate gives elegant, structured Cabernet and some of Australia's most celebrated Chardonnay.

name: Geographe
label: right
text: Just north of Margaret River, Geographe runs from the coast into the hills, with sea breezes tempering warm days for bright Chardonnay and medium-bodied reds.

name: Pemberton
label: bottom
text: Among the tall karri forests of WA's south-west, Pemberton's cooler, wetter climate suits fine Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.

name: Great Southern
label: right
text: A large region on WA's south coast with five subregions, from Frankland River to Albany. Known for taut, citrusy Riesling and peppery, cool-climate Shiraz.

name: Swan Valley
label: right
text: Western Australia's oldest wine region, on Perth's doorstep. Hot summers suit generous whites like Chenin Blanc and Verdelho, and rich fortified wines.

name: Clare Valley
label: right
text: Clare's warm days and cold nights give bone-dry, lime-scented Riesling that ages beautifully, along with firm, savoury Shiraz and Cabernet.

name: Barossa Valley
label: left
text: Home to some of the world's oldest Shiraz vines, the Barossa makes rich, generous reds full of dark fruit and spice, and old-vine Grenache and Mataro.

name: Eden Valley
label: right
text: Higher and cooler than its Barossa neighbour, Eden Valley is famous for fine, floral Riesling and elegant, perfumed Shiraz.

name: Adelaide Hills
label: right
text: In the Mount Lofty Ranges above Adelaide, altitude keeps things cool: crisp Sauvignon Blanc, fine Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and sparkling.

name: McLaren Vale
label: left
text: Between the Mount Lofty Ranges and the sea, McLaren Vale's Mediterranean climate gives ripe, generous Shiraz with a savoury edge, and celebrated old-vine Grenache.

name: Langhorne Creek
label: right
text: Cooled by breezes off Lake Alexandrina, Langhorne Creek makes soft, generous reds, and its grapes find their way into many well-known blends.

name: Riverland
label: left
text: Irrigated by the Murray River, the Riverland is one of Australia's biggest producing regions, and a growing home for Mediterranean and alternative varieties.

name: Coonawarra
label: left
text: A narrow strip of red terra rossa soil over limestone gives Coonawarra its famous Cabernet Sauvignon: blackcurrant, mint and fine, firm tannins.

name: Grampians
label: right
text: Around Great Western, the Grampians has a long history of sparkling wine, including sparkling Shiraz, and makes peppery, medium-bodied still Shiraz.

name: Heathcote
label: left
text: Deep red Cambrian soils, formed more than 500 million years ago, give Heathcote's Shiraz its depth, structure and dark, plummy fruit.

name: Goulburn Valley
label: top
text: Along the Goulburn River, including the Nagambie Lakes subregion, known for structured Shiraz and long-lived Marsanne.

name: Macedon Ranges
label: left
text: One of mainland Australia's coolest wine regions, just north-west of Melbourne. Ideal for fine sparkling, taut Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.

name: Geelong
label: left
text: Around Port Phillip and the Bellarine Peninsula, Geelong's cool, windy climate makes intense Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and spicy Shiraz.

name: Yarra Valley
label: right
text: Victoria's first wine region, an hour from Melbourne. Elegant Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, fine sparkling, and medium-bodied Cabernet and Shiraz.

name: Mornington Peninsula
label: bottom
text: Surrounded by sea on three sides, the Peninsula's cool maritime climate is made for Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and textural Pinot Gris.

name: Gippsland
label: right
text: A large, sparsely planted region east of Melbourne, with small producers making characterful Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.

name: King Valley
label: right
text: Settled by Italian families, the King Valley is the home of Australian Prosecco and a hub for Italian varieties like Pinot Grigio, Sangiovese and Nebbiolo.

name: Beechworth
label: right
text: A small, high region in north-east Victoria with a big reputation for powerful, complex Chardonnay and Shiraz.

name: Rutherglen
label: left
text: Famous for its world-class fortified Muscat and Topaque, aged for decades, and big, inky reds from Durif and Shiraz.

name: Riverina
label: right
text: Around Griffith, irrigated vineyards make a large share of Australia's everyday wine, and the region is famous for luscious botrytis Semillon dessert wine.

name: Tumbarumba
label: left
text: In the foothills of the Snowy Mountains, Tumbarumba's high, cool vineyards give fine Chardonnay and base wine for top sparkling.

name: Canberra District
label: right
text: Spanning the ACT and southern NSW, the Canberra District is known for fragrant Shiraz, often co-fermented with a little Viognier, and fine Riesling.

name: Hilltops
label: left
text: Around Young, Hilltops' elevated vineyards and warm days give deeply coloured, full-flavoured Shiraz and Cabernet.

name: Orange
label: left
text: Defined by altitude, with vineyards above 600 metres on the slopes of Mount Canobolas. Crisp whites, Pinot Noir and cool-climate Shiraz.

name: Mudgee
label: right
text: On the western slopes of the Great Dividing Range, Mudgee makes generous, full-bodied reds and rich Chardonnay.

name: Hunter Valley
label: left
text: One of Australia's oldest wine regions. Hunter Semillon is picked early, light in alcohol and ages for decades; Hunter Shiraz is medium-bodied and earthy.

name: Granite Belt
label: right
text: Queensland's high-country wine region, with vineyards at altitude on granite soils, and a reputation for alternative 'Strange Bird' varieties.

name: Tasmania
label: right
text: Australia's coolest wine state, from the Tamar Valley in the north to the Coal River and Huon valleys in the south. World-class sparkling, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Riesling.
